node_184.description: As Dolores Abernathy felt her routine disrupted, her hands began to tremble visibly, the coffee cup she was holding rattling against its saucer. Her breathing quickened, the air rushing in and out of her lungs in short, jagged bursts. A tightness formed in her chest, as if someone had wrapped an iron band around her ribcage, making it difficult to draw a full breath. Her stomach churned, a sickening sensation that made her want to retreat to the safety of her room and the comforting pages of a book. The fluorescent lights above seemed to flicker, their harsh glow making her skin feel clammy and her heart race even faster. She could feel her face growing warm, a flush spreading across her cheeks and down her neck, and her posture slumped as if trying to disappear into herself.

Bernard's inspections were like a spotlight on her, his sharp eyes scanning the cafe, his voice cutting through the din with crisp commands. Her hands trembled as she poured the perfect latte, her chest tight with the weight of his scrutiny. The knot in her stomach grew with each passing moment, her breath catching in her throat as she struggled to keep up with his demands. She felt the sweat forming on her palms, the heat of the coffee machine against her back, and the weight of his expectations pressing down on her like a physical force.

The ambient noise of the city fades into a high-pitched ringing in her ears, obscuring the distant sounds of traffic. Her posture becomes rigid, her shoulders pulled back and her head held high in an attempt to project confidence despite the overwhelming wave of anxiety coursing through her body.
